Article 9

1. The obligations and responsibilities of the community as referred to in Article 7 letter b, shall be implemented in the form of community participation.
2. The form of community participation as referred to in paragraph (1), includes:
a. preventing the occurrence of acts of violence against women and children;
b. providing protection to women and children from acts of violence;
c. providing information and/or reporting acts of violence against women and children to law enforcement or authorized parties; and
d. participating in the handling of victims of acts of violence.
3. The form of community participation as referred to in paragraph (2), shall be implemented responsibly in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regent Regulation, the following terms shall mean:

1. Region is Pohuwato Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of the Regional Government administration who leads the implementation of governmental affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region.
3. Regent is the Regent of Pohuwato.
4. Regional House of Representatives, hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD, is a regional people's representative institution positioned as an element of Regional Government administration.
5. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent and DPRD in administering governmental affairs that are the authority of the Region.
6. Regional Long-Term Development Plan, hereinafter abbreviated as RPJPD, is a regional planning document for a period of 20 (twenty) years.
7. Regional Medium-Term Development Plan, hereinafter abbreviated as RPJMD, is a regional planning document for a period of 5 (five) years.
8. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to victims carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination.
9. Violence is any act unlawfully with or without the use of means against physical and verbal that causes danger to life, body and/or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom.
10. Violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life.
11. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child.
12. Discrimination is any distinction, harassment or exclusion that is direct or indirect based on human differentiation on the basis of religion, ethnicity, race, ethnic group, social status, economic status, gender, language, political beliefs that results in reduction, deviation or elimination of recognition, implementation or use of human rights and basic freedoms in life both individually and collectively in the political, economic, legal, social, cultural and other aspects of life.
13. Trafficking in Persons is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt of a person by threat of violence, use of violence, abduction, confinement, forgery, fraud and abuse of power or vulnerable position, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether carried out within the country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the person being exploited.
14. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years including a child still in the womb.
15. Victim of violence is a woman and child who experiences suffering whether physical, mental or emotional, economic loss, or experiences neglect, reduction or deprivation of their basic rights.
16. Prevention is direct efforts carried out by the Regional Government and/or community to prevent the occurrence of acts of violence against women and children.
17. Integrated Service Center, hereinafter abbreviated as PPT, is an Integrated Service Unit established by the Regional Government to provide services and rehabilitation to women and children who are victims of violence comprehensively including information services, assistance and legal aid, counseling services, medical services and safe houses through referral.
18. Task Force for the Prevention and Handling of Criminal Acts of Trafficking in Persons, hereinafter referred to as the Task Force, is a coordinating institution tasked with coordinating prevention and handling efforts of criminal acts of trafficking in persons in Pohuwato Regency.
19. Safe house is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with determined operational standards.
20. Social reintegration is the process of preparing the community and victims that supports reunification into the family environment, school environment, work environment and community environment that can provide protection and fulfillment of victims' needs.
21. Victim recovery is services provided in the form of strengthening and developing the capacity of a person who experiences acts of violence against women and children to be more empowered physically, psychologically, sexually, economically and socially.
22. Assistance is all actions in the form of counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy and spiritual guidance, for the purpose of self-empowerment of women and children from acts of violence to resolve the problems faced.
23. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband and wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in direct line upward or downward to the third degree.
24. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or step father and/or mother, or adoptive father and/or mother.
25. Community is individuals, families, groups, and social organizations and/or community organizations.

CHAPTER VI

INSTITUTIONAL ARRANGEMENTS

Article 11

1. The Regional Government establishes an Integrated Service Center (PPT) in providing protection to women and children from acts of violence.
2. The PPT as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be established at the Regency and Sub-district levels.
3. The membership of the PPT as referred to in paragraph (1) consists of elements of the Regional Government, law enforcement, community organizations, non-governmental organizations, professional organizations, researchers and academics.
4. Further provisions regarding the Organization and Working Procedures of the PPT as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be regulated by Regent Regulation.

CHAPTER V

OBLIGATIONS AND RESPONSIBILITIES

Article 7

Obligations and responsibilities in providing protection to women and children from acts of violence are the shared responsibility of:
a. Regional Government;
b. Community.

Article 27

1. The Regional Government may provide financial assistance to community organizations, social organizations or non-governmental organizations that implement protection of women and children from discrimination and acts of violence.
2. Financial assistance as referred to in paragraph (1), is in accordance with regional financial capacity, and is implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations in the field of regional finance.

Article 24

The community may conduct supervision of the implementation of protection of women and children from acts of violence organized by the Regional Government with a mechanism for conveying aspirations to the Regent or to the DPRD.

Article 19

Coordination includes:
a. Conducting coordination and cooperation in handling cases of violence with integrated service institutions;
b. Conducting coordination and cooperation in handling cases of violence with integrated services between regions.

Article 12

In addition to establishing the PPT as referred to in Article 11, in order to support the implementation of the provision of protection to women and children from acts of violence, the Regent establishes:
a. Task force on trafficking in persons;
b. Regional action committee for the elimination of the worst forms of child labor.
